newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease in continued correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease in continued correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped slightly in weaker volume on Friday in continued correction, but recovered from lows on mild support that emerged after Thursday's 3.7 percent plunge, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed down 361.74 points, or 0.47 percent at 76,210.51 after twice rebounding from slightly below the 76,000 mark. Trade volume dived to 12.08 trillion lira ($129.4 million) from 18.6 trillion ($199 million) on Thursday.
"76,000 is an important level. If the market opens lower on Monday, the easing may continue towards 73,500-74,000 range," said Murat Emrali from Eczacibasi securities.
"But if it bottoms out at 76,000-76,500 and turns up, it will face resistance at 77,500 and then drift sideways for a while," he added.

Brokers said the market would be tuned to political developments next week when the parliament will pick up a censure motion against Prime Minister Erbakan on October 16 for his controversial trip to Libya last week.

Thursday's plunge was the first major correction to the latest uptrend during which the index rocketed 22.7 percent from September 13 to Wednesday's sixth consequtive all-time high close of 79,511.82.
Over the week, the index lost 0.63 percent after last week's 7.15 percent jump.
